Every year, Apple runs a "Back to School" student promotion, offering special deals on Mac or iPad purchases during the promotional period. Past offers have typically included free accessories like AirPods or Apple gift cards valued between $100 and $150. According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, the offer will return later this week.

The promotion usually begins around this time, but Apple has delayed its launch due to significant price increases caused by a memory shortage.

However, Gurman noted that Apple is reportedly setting up related promotional materials at retail stores "mid-week," so the offer should officially launch sometime this week.

It remains unclear whether this year's offer will be more attractive than previous ones. With Mac and iPad prices rising significantly, Apple may need to step up the incentive to make the new pricing more palatable for students.

It's also worth noting that the company recently added UNiDAYs student verification to its U.S. Education Store, meaning those who don't verify their status will no longer be able to take advantage of the offer.

What Apple has in store is still unknown. Hopefully, even with the steep price hikes, the promotion will still be attractive enough to entice students to buy.
